decisions.reason: Selecting the Business Case site list does not change the full-network opex requirement. The separate opex decision in the same message is already represented by the candidate's own MODIFY.

The authoritative site list determines network membership but does not alter the candidate's capex assumption basis, site typologies, or existing twelve-site scope. No stale site-list attribute exists in this candidate.

The program-wide cost categories and their presentation as separate capex line items remain unchanged by selecting the Business Case site list. Their introduction comes from a separate clause in the same message.
The selected site list does not change the financing shares, interest-rate assumption, or tranche structure. The financing decision in message 23 is independently represented by the existing MODIFY.

Choosing the Business Case site list does not change the AUD model currency or 2031 price base. The candidate's currency ambiguity arises from the separate CAD-denominated opex decision, not from the site-list decision.
The authoritative site list does not change the requirement to calculate equity IRR against the 16–20% target. That target is established by a separate clause in message 23.
Selecting the site list does not change the required asset-appropriate CCA treatment, example classes, tax-shield modeling, or treatment of equity-return effects.
The source decision does not add, remove, or change any modeled revenue stream or the requirement to model the streams separately.
The choice of authoritative sites does not change the requirement to retain an integrated three-statement model structure.

The site-list decision does not change the DSCR and equity-IRR sizing targets. The availability-payment rules are established by a separate clause in message 23 and are already represented by the candidate's MODIFY.
The source decision does not change the requirement to maintain the debt schedule or produce DSCR coverage analysis.
Selecting the Business Case site list does not alter the Case F and Case G definitions, the availability-payment mechanism, or the requirement to compare the scenarios.
